title: Microplastics in water aren’t inert and make damaging chemicals on their own
abstract: One reason plastics are used so often is that they’re chemically inert, meaning bags, food containers, and cups don't react with what we put in them. Yet they can still break down into microplastics, which turn up in drinking water, human blood, arteries, and brains. The consequences of that are uncertain. “Whether microplastics can directly cause human disease is still being researched,” said Wei Min, a chemist at Columbia University. In a new Nature study, Min's team took a step toward answering this question by demonstrating that microplastics are likely not as chemically inert as we might expect. Microdroplet chemistry Min's lab has spent years working on microdroplet chemistry, studying how water broken into tiny droplets behaves at its boundary with air. These droplets have been reported to generate reactive oxygen species, or ROS, a family of harmful, oxygen-containing molecules. “ROS will essentially bump into proteins, lipids, DNA, and cause damage,” Min said. “You could break a DNA strand into segments. You could mutate DNA; you could misfold proteins.” Read full article Comments

title: Katie Zacharia Was Linked to an AI Rare-Earths Startup. It’s Even Weirder Than It Sounds
abstract: The short-lived White House press secretary was listed as an adviser to a Kristi Noem–linked company that aims to use AI for mining. Both the company and she say she never worked there.

title: Maybe Chatbots Shouldn’t Get to Say ‘I’ or ‘Me’

abstract: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we dive into an unexpected Muse feature, shadowy spending from the largest pro-AI super PAC, and men’s tendency to lie about how much they know about AI.

title: 실행은 도메인별로, 문맥은 한 레포에
abstract: 들어가며 안녕하세요, 토스 Data Warehouse 팀의 Data Analytics Engineer 김문수입니다. 이 글에서는 데이터 웨어하우스(DW) 마트를 만드는 중앙 DW Airflow를 멈추지 않고, 도메인별 DW Airflow와 dbt 기반의 선언적 파이프라인으로 옮겨 온 과정을 공유하려고 합니다. 새 플랫폼은 팀 안에서 이를 ‘뉴타운’이라고 부르고 있습니다. 얼마 전 코딩 에이전트에게 "이 테이블 어디서 만들어져?"라고 물었습니다. 한참 코드를 뒤지던 에이전트의 답은 이랬습니다. "적재 주체는 코드에 없어 확인할 수 없습니다." 맞는 말입니다. 정말로 코드에 없었기 때문이죠. 이 글은 그 답을 코드에 적어 넣기까지의 이야기입니다. 그 과정에서 토스 광고 도메인의 DAG 코드는 2,794줄에서 100줄 이 되었고, 테이블 순서를 손으로 잇던 >> 180줄은 0줄 이 되었습니다. 파이프라인 시간도 4시간에서 2시간 30분 으로 줄었습니다. DW Airflow 하나에 DAG 400여 개 토스에는 용도와 팀에 따라 운영하는 Airflow가 여럿 있습니다. 이 글에서 다루는 건 그중 DW 마트를 만드는 DW Airflow입니다. DW 마트에는 광고, 쇼핑, 결제, 금융 등 도메인 팀이 각자 관리하는 도메인 마트와, 중앙 DW팀이 관리하는 마트가 있습니다. 중앙 DW팀은 전사 공통 마트뿐 아니라, 어느 도메인에도 딱 떨어지지 않아 주인이 애매한 마트까지 맡고 있습니다. 그런데 이 마트 파이프라인이 도메인과 상관없이 전부 DW Airflow 클러스터 하나에서 돌고 있었습니다. DAG 파일로 세면 400개가 넘습니다. 한 클러스터에 모여 있다 보니 문제가 몇 가지 있었습니다. 한 도메인의 배치가 몰리면 다른 도메인의 배치까지 밀렸고, 파이프라인 하나를 고치려면 다른 도메인이 어떻게 돌고 있는지까지 알아야 했습니다. 비슷한 로직도 표준 없이 여기저기 복사돼 있었습니다. 매일 겪는 불편은 조금 더 구체적이었습니다. 테이블 하나를 이해하려면 다섯 군데를 열어야 했습니다. 어느 DAG에서 어떤 순서로 도는지: DAG 파일 어떻게 만드는지: SQL 파일 품질 규칙: 별도 설정 파일이나 품질 관리 시스템 테이블과 컬럼 설명: 사내 데이터 카탈로그 읽는 테이블이 어디서 만들어지는지: 원천 DB에서 적재한 테이블이면 적재 메타 관리 시스템, 다른 마트면 영향도 시스템 등 여러 사내 시스템 고쳐 쓰지 않고 옆에 새로 짓기로 했습니다 처음에는 기존 레포를 리팩토링하는 방법도 생각했습니다. 그런데 문제의 뿌리가 "클러스터 하나에 다 모여 있다"는 구조 자체라서, 코드를 아무리 정리해도 이 부분은 해결이 안 됩니다. 그렇다고 전사 배치를 한 번에 새 플랫폼으로 옮기는 건 너무 위험합니다. 문제가 생기면 대응하기가 꽤 까다로워요. 돌이킬 수 있으면서 간편한 방식을 원했습니다. 그래서 기존 시스템 옆에 새 시스템을 짓고, 기능을 하나씩 옮긴 뒤 옮긴 부분만 기존 시스템에서 걷어내는 방식을 택했습니다. 이걸 부르는 이름이 있을 것 같아 찾아보니 Strangler Fig 방식이라고 하더라고요. 교살 무화과나무가 숙주 나무를 감싸며 자라다가 결국 기존 나무를 대체하는 자연현상에서 유래했다고 합니다. (이름이 무서운 나무네요.) 아무튼 기존 파이프라인은 마지막 순간까지 그대로 돌고, 옮기다 문제가 생기면 언제든 되돌릴 수 있습니다. 옮기는 단위를 도메인으로 잡았기 때문에, 언제, 얼마나 옮길지는 도메인 팀이 정할 수 있었습니다. 같은 데이터를 하루에 두 번 만들었습니다 플랫폼이 어느정도 만들어졌을 때, 적당한 마이그레이션 대상을 찾고 있었는데요. 마침 찾은 이 마트 DAG은 주인이 따로 없고, 마지막 변경이 1년이 넘었고, TASK의 수도 적당했습니다. 7월 말에 이 마트를 옮겨 둔 도메인의 main DAG에 13시 대기 sensor와 이 마트의 트리거를 추가했습니다. 기존 파이프라인은 평소처럼 새벽에 돌고, 뉴타운은 같은 날 13시에 같은 데이터를 한 번 더 만듭니다. 같은 데이터를 하루에 두 번 만드는 건 낭비 같지만, 가장 싼 보험이었습니다. 이렇게 3주 동안 두 결과를 비교했습니다. 8월 20일에 검증이 끝났다고 보고, 13시 대기를 빼서 새벽에 돌게 하는 PR을 머지했습니다. 그런데 같은 날 저녁 revert했습니다. 문제가 생긴 건 아니고, 기존 파이프라인 쪽 준비가 더 필요했기 때문입니다. 기존 DW Airflow에는 테이블간의 audit 기반으로 만든 영향도를 보고 앞 단계를 기다리는 sensor가 있어서, 이 마트를 뉴타운 쪽 결과로 바라보게 바꾸는 작업을 따로 해야 했습니다. 그래서 다음 주로 미뤘습니다. revert 커밋 메시지는 ‘다음주에 하는걸로’ 한 줄이었고, 실제로 8월 24일에 다시 머지했습니다. 그동안 기존 파이프라인은 계속 새벽에 돌고 있었으니 데이터를 쓰는 쪽에서는 아무 일도 없었습니다. 한 번에 옮기는 방식이었다면 이 일정 조정은 꽤 큰 롤백 작업이 됐을 겁니다. 광고 도메인을 옮길 때도 같은 방식으로 두 파이프라인을 나란히 돌리며 결과를 비교한 뒤 넘겼습니다. 반대로 하지 않기로 한 것도 있습니다. Spark 잡은 dbt로 바꾸지 않았고, Jenkins 잡도 당장 없애지 않고 이어 쓰되 새로 만드는 것만 막았습니다. 다 할 수는 있는 일이지만, 전부 새 방식으로 바꾸려고 하면 이주가 늦어지고 두 플랫폼을 같이 운영하는 기간만 길어집니다. 같은 이유로 기존의 모델 레이어 구성 방식을 바꾸는 것도 이관 이후에 하는 걸 권장했어요. 도메인별 클러스터와 dbt 새 플랫폼에서는 DW Airflow를 도메인별로 나눴습니다. 도메인마다 자기 DW Airflow 클러스터를 갖는 구조로, 지금은 ads, foundation, finops, fmd, dw-core까지 5개 클러스터가 있습니다. 다만 기존 파이프라인을 대규모로 옮겨 온 건 아직 광고(ads) 한 곳이고, 나머지는 새로 만드는 마트나 옮기기 위한 준비 위주로 쓰이고 있습니다. 도메인 팀이 자기 파이프라인을 책임지려면, 다른 도메인의 배포나 장애에 흔들리지 않는 실행 환경이 있어야 한다고 봤습니다. 코드는 레포 하나에 두고, 공통 모듈은 플랫폼팀이, 도메인 디렉토리는 각 도메인 팀이 관리합니다. 물론 공통 모듈에 기여하는 건 누구나 할 수 있습니다. 변환 로직은 Impala에 직접 날리던 쿼리에서 dbt 모델로 옮겼습니다. dbt는 SELECT 문만 적으면 테이블 생성과 적재를 대신 해 주고, 모델 사이의 의존 관계를 그래프로 관리해 주는 도구입니다. dbt 모델을 Airflow task로 펼치는 데는 흔히 쓰는 Cosmos를 썼고, 모델 하나가 task 하나가 됩니다. dbt만으로는 Spark 잡이나 다른 클러스터의 테이블을 기다리는 sensor를 표현할 수 없어서, 선언만 해 두면 이런 task와 의존성을 자동으로 만들어 주는 wrapper를 따로 만들었습니다. 이 wrapper가 실제로 무엇을 읽고 무엇을 만드는지는 아래 ‘나머지는 yml에’ 문단에서 보여 드리겠습니다. 클러스터를 나누니 새로운 문제도 생겼습니다. 클러스터 하나일 때는 손쉽게 해결됐던 DAG 간 의존이, 클러스터를 건너는 의존이 된 것입니다. 이건 두 가지로 풀었습니다. 도메인마다 스케줄을 가진 main DAG를 하나만 두고 나머지 DAG는 main이 trigger하게 해서, 모두 같은 날짜를 공유하게 했습니다. 기존 DW Airflow에서도 쓰던 패턴이라 팀원들이 익숙하게 받아들일 수 있었습니다. 그리고 다른 곳에서 만드는 테이블은 만들어지는 방식에 따라 기다리는 방법을 나눴습니다. 원천 DB에서 적재하는 테이블은 적재 상태가 적재 시스템의 백엔드 서버에 메타로 기록되고 있어서, ‘오늘 적재됐는가’를 그 기록에서 직접 확인할 수 있었습니다. 기존 DW Airflow에서 만드는 마트는 그 테이블을 만드는 Airflow task가 끝났는지를 봅니다. SQL에는 로직만 남겼습니다 기존 SQL과 옮긴 뒤의 SQL을 간단히 비교하면 이렇습니다. (예시를 위해 단순화했습니다.) insert overwrite 같은 적재 구문은 사라지고, 읽는 테이블 이름이 ref() 로 바뀝니다. 비즈니스 로직은 그대로입니다. 대

title: 토스뱅크가 패키지를 관리하는 방식 #2: 토스뱅크 패키지의 세 가지 기준
abstract: 안녕하세요. 토스뱅크에서 패키지 개발 환경을 개선하고 있는 기술그룹입니다. 패키지를 사용하는 쪽(이하 호스트)에서는 패키지 코드가 어떤 브라우저까지 지원하는지, 패키지 개발 중 사용하던 API를 실행 환경에서도 쓸 수 있는지 따로 살펴봐야 했어요. 호스트에서 패키지의 원본 소스 코드를 확인하기도 어려웠어요. 이 문제를 해결하기 위해 패키지가 갖춰야 할 기준을 정했어요. 그리고 각 기준을 충족하려면 무엇이 필요한지 살펴보고, 그에 맞는 빌드 도구와 설정을 선택하기로 했어요. 기준은 세 가지예요. 안정성 : 호스트가 지원하는 실행 환경에서 안정적으로 동작해야 해요. 예측 가능성 : 배포 후에도 원본 코드의 의도가 유지되어야 해요. 디버깅 편의성 : 사용처에서 쉽게 디버깅할 수 있어야 해요. 호스트가 지원하는 실행 환경에서 안정적으로 동작해야 해요 토스뱅크의 각 서비스는 자신의 지원 범위에 맞춰 패키지를 항상 트랜스파일해요. 그럼 최신 문법을 모두 사용해도 호스트 런타임에 문제가 없다고 보장할 수 있을까요? 문법은 호스트의 트랜스파일러가 해당 문법 변환을 지원해야 하고, API는 실행 환경에서 제공하거나 폴리필로 추가해야 해요. 예를 들어 rolldown의 문법 변환 관련 이슈 에서는 당시 oxc가 ES2025의 일부 정규식 문법을 구형 환경용으로 변환하지 못한다는 점을 짚었어요. 즉 최종 호스트가 낮은 target 을 지정하더라도 도구가 지원하지 않는 변환까지 수행되지는 않는 거예요. 폴리필에도 한계가 있어요. 예를 들어 Proxy 는 이를 지원하지 않는 엔진에서 폴리필만으로 전체 동작을 구현할 수 없어요. 폴리필 라이브러리를 추가하는 것만으로 모든 API를 사용할 수 있게 되는 것은 아니에요. 따라서 문법은 호스트의 변환 도구가 처리할 수 있는지, API는 대상 브라우저 또는 호스트의 폴리필이 제공할 수 있는지를 각각 확인해야 해요. 트랜스파일링을 호스트에 맡기더라도 호환성 문제는 패키지 개발 단계에서 미리 확인해야 해요. 그래서 호스트의 API 지원 범위를 타입 검사에 반영했어요. 다만 TypeScript 설정만으로 호환성을 모두 확인할 수는 없으므로, 실제 API 지원 여부와 필요한 문법 변환이 가능한지도 확인해야 해요. 배포 후에도 원본 코드의 의도가 유지되어야 해요 호스트는 자신의 실행 환경에 맞춰 패키지 코드를 변환하고 번들링해요. 저희는 이 작업을 호스트에 맡기고, 패키지 빌드에서는 원본의 문법과 모듈 구조를 최대한 유지하기로 했어요. 문법 변환은 호스트에 맡겨요 패키지를 사용하는 서비스마다 지원하는 브라우저와 런타임이 달라요. 따라서 같은 패키지 코드라도 호스트에 따라 필요한 문법 변환이 달라질 수 있어요. 예를 들어 user?.name 을 Optional Chaining을 지원하지 않는 환경에 맞춰 변환하면 다음처럼 바뀔 수 있어요. 이 상태로 패키지를 배포하면 Optional Chaining을 지원하는 호스트도 변환된 코드를 받게 돼요. 문법에 따라서는 호환성을 위한 함수가 추가되기도 해요. 패키지에서 문법을 미리 낮추면 호스트에 필요하지 않은 코드가 포함되고, 원본과 결과물의 차이도 커져요. 그래서 저희는 패키지의 JavaScript 문법을 유지하고, 실행 환경에 맞춘 문법 변환은 호스트에 맡기기로 했어요. 호스트가 자신의 지원 범위에 맞춰 필요한 변환을 적용하도록 했어요. 모듈 구조도 유지해 전달해요 패키지를 빌드할 때 미리 번들링하면, 원본에서 나눠 둔 파일의 경계가 달라질 수 있어요. 프레임워크가 파일 단위로 코드를 처리하는 경우에는 이 차이가 실제 동작에도 영향을 줄 수 있어요. 예를 들어 Next.js App Router에서는 'use client' 를 선언한 파일이 클라이언트 코드의 경계가 돼요. 이 선언이 있는 Counter.tsx 와 선언이 없는 formatPrice.ts 가 분리돼 있다면, Server Component에서도 formatPrice 를 가져와 호출할 수 있어요. 하지만 두 파일을 하나로 번들링하고 전체에 'use client' 를 적용하면, formatPrice 도 클라이언트 코드로 처리돼 같은 방식으로 호출할 수 없어요. 번들링 과정에서도 이런 경계를 유지할 수 있어요. 다만 패키지 빌드에서 파일별 지시문의 적용 범위까지 고려해야 하고, 이를 위한 설정도 관리해야 해요. 그래서 저희는 원본의 모듈 구조를 유지해 배포하기로 했어요. 호스트가 파일별 지시문과 모듈 경계를 해석할 수 있도록 전달하고, 최종 번들링은 호스트에 맡겼어요. 패키지 빌드에서는 TypeScript를 JavaScript로 변환하고, 실행 환경에 맞춘 문법 변환과 최종 번들링은 호스트가 담당하도록 했어요. 사용처에서 쉽게 디버깅할 수 있어야 해요 패키지가 예상과 다르게 동작하면 사용하는 서비스에서도 원인을 파악할 수 있어야 해요. 함수가 어떤 조건에서 오류를 던지는지, 옵션을 생략하면 어떻게 동작하는지 확인하려면 타입 선언과 문서만으로는 부족할 수 있어요. 이때 가장 빠른 방법은 원본 코드를 직접 확인하는 거예요. 그래서 에디터에서 패키지의 원본 코드를 바로 확인할 수 있도록 declaration sourcemap을 지원하기로 했어요. declaration sourcemap은 .d.ts 의 각 선언을 원본 소스의 해당 위치와 연결해 주는 파일이에요. 이 파일과 원본 파일을 설치된 패키지에 포함하면, 사용하는 쪽에서도 IDE에서 클릭 한 번으로 d.ts 대신 실제 구현을 확인할 수 있어요. 마치며 호스트의 지원 범위에 맞춰 패키지를 개발하고, 문법과 모듈 구조를 유지해 배포하도록 기준을 정했어요. 사용하는 쪽에서는 자신의 환경에 맞춰 문법 변환과 번들링을 진행하고, 문제가 생기면 설치된 패키지의 원본 구현을 바로 확인할 수 있도록 했어요. 저희 기술그룹은 안정성, 예측 가능성, 디버깅 편의성을 기준으로 패키지를 만드는 쪽과 사용하는 쪽의 역할을 정리했어요. 이 기준 덕분에 빌드 도구와 설정을 선택할 때도, 어떤 변환이 필요하고 어떤 파일을 제공해야 하는지 일관되게 판단할 수 있게 됐어요.

title: 토스뱅크가 패키지를 관리하는 방식 #1: 패키지를 ESM으로만 제공하기로 했어요
abstract: 안녕하세요. 토스뱅크에서 패키지 개발 환경을 개선하고 있는 기술그룹입니다. 토스뱅크에서는 여러 서비스가 함께 쓰는 코드를 패키지로 관리해요. 그동안 ECMAScript Modules(이하 ESM)와 CommonJS(이하 CJS) 두 형식으로 빌드하고, package.json 의 exports 로 각 환경에 맞는 코드와 타입을 제공해왔어요. 이러한 Dual package 방식의 배경과 설정은 CommonJS와 ESM에 모두 대응하는 라이브러리 개발하기: exports field 에서 자세히 볼 수 있어요. 그런데 Dual package 방식은 두 형식으로 빌드하는 것 외에도 신경 쓸 일이 많았어요. 같은 패키지의 상태가 둘로 나뉘거나, 한쪽 경로에서 타입을 찾지 못할 수 있었거든요. 어떤 문제인지부터 살펴볼게요. 같은 패키지인데 상태가 둘로 나뉘어요 React 컨텍스트를 제공하는 패키지를 ESM과 CJS로 각각 빌드했다고 해볼게요. 서비스는 ESM 구현을, 서비스가 사용하는 다른 패키지는 CJS 구현을 읽는 상황이에요. 두 구현에서 각각 컨텍스트를 만들면 객체도 둘이 돼요. 서비스의 Provider는 컨텍스트 ①에 값을 넣는데, 다른 패키지의 Hook은 컨텍스트 ②에서 값을 찾을 수 있어요. Provider로 감쌌는데도 값을 읽지 못하는 거예요. 같은 패키지 이름으로 불렀는데 왜 이런 일이 생길까요? exports 에서 불러오는 방식에 따라 서로 다른 파일을 연결했기 때문이에요. 이 구성에서는 import 와 require() 가 서로 다른 구현을 읽어요. 두 모듈이 각각 실행되면서 만든 객체는 내용이 같아도 다른 객체예요. 패키지를 한 버전만 설치했어도 생길 수 있는 일이에요. 이렇게 두 모듈이 함께 로드되면서 공유해야 할 객체나 상태가 나뉘는 위험을 Dual package hazard 라고 해요. 컨텍스트뿐 아니라 모듈이 보관하는 캐시나 상태도 영향을 받을 수 있어요. 실행 코드는 찾았는데 타입은 찾지 못해요 타입도 두 경로에서 확인해야 해요. 우리 패키지의 타입이 외부 라이브러리를 참조한다면, 그 라이브러리의 타입까지 올바르게 연결돼야 하고요. 예를 들어 UI 패키지가 외부 라이브러리의 ExternalProps 를 가져와 버튼의 props를 정의한다고 해볼게요. TypeScript는 외부 라이브러리의 package.json에 명시된 exports를 따라 타입을 찾아요. 이때 TypeScript 설정에 따라 import(ESM) 또는 require(CJS) 경로를 선택할 수 있어요. CJS 경로를 선택했는데 타입 파일이 명시돼 있지 않고, 대응하는 파일도 없다면 타입을 찾지 못할 수 있어요. 타입을 찾지 못해 ExternalProps 가 any 로 처리되면, ButtonProps 도 any 가 돼요. 사용처에서 잘못된 props를 넘겨도 타입 에러가 나지 않아 문제를 놓칠 수 있어요. ( TypeScript 문서 ) 개발과 디버깅이 복잡해져요 만드는 쪽에서는 패키지나 의존성이 바뀔 때마다 두 경로의 실행 코드와 타입 연결을 확인해야 해요. 사용하는 쪽에서도 문제가 생기면 어느 구현이 로드됐고 어떤 타입을 읽었는지부터 추적해야 해요. 코드가 같아 보여도 실행 경로가 달라질 수 있어 디버깅이 복잡해져요. 패키지를 만들고 쓰는 일을 단순하게 하려면, 두 형식을 계속 제공해야 하는지부터 살펴봐야 했어요. ESM-only를 선택했어요 두 형식을 제공했던 가장 큰 이유는 CJS 사용처를 지원하기 위해서였어요. 과거 Node.js에서는 CJS의 require() 로 ESM을 불러올 수 없었거든요. 그런데 Node.js 22.12.0부터는 별도 플래그 없이 require(esm) 을 지원해요 . CJS 코드에서도 ESM을 불러올 수 있게 된 거예요. 이때 불러오는 ESM과 의존 모듈에는 최상위 await 가 없어야 해요. Node.js의 변화에 맞춰 JavaScript 생태계에서도 ESM-only를 지원하는 흐름이 이어지고 있었어요. 그런데도 왜 여전히 dual package로 제공하는 라이브러리가 많을까요? 공개 라이브러리는 구버전 Node.js를 포함한 다양한 환경에서 사용돼요. 이런 사용처까지 지원하려면 ESM과 CJS를 함께 제공해야 할 수 있어요. 저희 패키지는 사내에서만 사용하기 때문에 사용처를 파악하고 지원 환경도 함께 조정할 수 있었어요. 이처럼 예측 가능한 환경에서는 하나의 형식만 제공해도 충분하다고 판단했어요. ESM을 고른 가장 큰 이유는 JavaScript의 표준 모듈 시스템이기 때문이에요. 트리 셰이킹에도 유리하고요. 저희는 도구 버전과 설정을 맞추고, 패키지를 불러오는 코드와 타입 검사를 확인하며 ESM-only로 전환했어요. 평소 도구를 꾸준히 최신화해온 것이 도움이 됐어요. 마치며 ESM-only 전환으로 패키지를 만드는 쪽은 두 구현의 코드와 타입을 함께 관리할 부담을 덜었어요. 사용하는 쪽에서도 어느 구현이 로드됐는지 추적할 일이 줄었고요. 저희 기술그룹은 ESM-only 전환을 포함해 패키지를 더 단순하고 안정적으로 개발하기 위한 기준을 정리했어요. 다음 글에서는 이 기준을 어떻게 정했는지, 타입과 원본 소스를 어떻게 제공하고 빌드를 구성했는지 이어서 소개할게요.

title: Spark Connect on Kubernetes #2: Operator로 만드는 Control Plane
abstract: 안녕하세요. 토스증권 Data Infra팀 박지원입니다. 지난 편 에서는 Spark Connect 서버를 여러 replica로 나누고 Gateway로 요청을 분산시켰습니다. 한 Driver에 몰리던 사용자를 분산해 장애와 리소스 경합을 줄이기 위해 새 세션은 한가한 서버에 배치하고, 기존 세션은 원래 서버로 보냈어요. 그런데 Gateway가 요청을 보낼 서버들은 누가 만들고 관리할까요? Driver가 죽으면 다시 띄워야 하고, 이미지나 설정을 바꾸려면 실행 중인 서버를 교체해야 해요. 이미 세션이 붙어 있는 서버를 그냥 내릴 수는 없고요. 이번 편은 이 서버들의 생명주기를 관리하는 Control Plane 이야기입니다. 개별 서버의 실행과 복구는 Apache Spark Operator에 맡기고, 여러 서버를 하나의 서비스로 운영하는 Spark Tenant Operator를 만들었어요. 두 계층의 역할과 서버 교체 과정을 살펴본 뒤, 장기 실행 중 겪은 Driver 메모리 문제도 다룰게요. 여러 Spark Connect 서버를 어떻게 관리할까 대화형 분석과 무거운 파이프라인을 같은 서버에서 실행하면 자원 경합이 생겨요. 그래서 용도별로 서버를 묶고 이미지, 자원, Spark 설정과 replica 수를 지정했어요. 이 서버 그룹을 테넌트 라고 부릅니다. 아래 표는 용도에 따라 테넌트 설정을 나눈 예시예요. 구분 테넌트 A 테넌트 B 용도 대화형 분석 대용량 파이프라인 Driver 사양(CPU / Heap) 2 cores / 4 GiB 4 cores / 8 GiB Executor 사양(CPU / Heap) 2 cores / 4 GiB 4 cores / 16 GiB spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors 10 50 spark.sql.shuffle.partitions 200 1000 두 Operator의 역할 나누기 테넌트를 운영하려면 개별 서버의 장애를 복구하고 테넌트 전체의 서버 수를 유지해야 해요. 스펙이나 설정이 바뀌면 서버를 교체해야 하고요. 저희는 이 역할을 두 Operator로 나눴습니다. Kubernetes에서 Deployment가 여러 Pod의 수와 교체를 관리하는 것처럼, 저희는 Spark Tenant Operator가 여러 SparkApplication을 관리해요. SparkTenant 에 원하는 설정과 서버 수를 선언하면 Tenant Operator가 그에 맞춰 SparkApplication을 생성하고 교체해요. 각 Application의 Driver를 실행하고 상태를 관측하며 실패 시 복구하는 일은 Apache Spark Operator가 맡습니다. 단일 서버의 기동과 복구는 Apache Spark Operator로 Driver Pod가 생성된 뒤에도 이미지 pull과 프로세스 시작, Spark 초기화를 거쳐야 Connect 요청을 받을 수 있어요. 이 과정에서 실패할 수도 있고, 요청을 처리하던 Driver가 종료될 수도 있습니다. Apache Spark Operator는 기동 상태를 관측하고 단계별로 상태를 관리해요. 저희는 실패 시 정해진 한도 안에서 Driver를 새로 생성하도록 구성했습니다. 같은 SparkApplication 안에서 새 attempt가 시작되며, 기존 세션은 복원되지 않아요. 주요 상태와 재시작 경로를 단순화한 그림입니다. 실패는 기동 중에도 발생할 수 있어요. DriverReady 이후에는 Executor 확보 상태에 따라 RunningHealthy 등으로 변경됩니다. Apache Spark Operator의 재시도가 끝나면 Tenant Operator가 종료된 Application을 삭제하고 새로 생성해요. 다만 drain 중이 아닌 정상 서버가 하나 이상 남아 있을 때만 진행하며, 하나도 없으면 장애로 판단하고 자동 교체를 보류해요. 새 Application을 계속 만들어 Apache Spark Operator의 재시도 한도를 우회하면, 같은 실패가 끝없이 반복될 수 있기 때문이에요. 준비된 서버로 전환하고 기존 세션 마무리하기 서버가 정상적으로 실행 중이어도 교체가 필요한 때가 있어요. Spark 버전을 올리거나 Driver 메모리를 늘리는 경우입니다. 테넌트 설정을 바꾸면 Tenant Operator가 변경된 설정으로 새 서버들을 준비해요. 문제는 기존 서버에서 사용자가 여전히 작업하고 있다는 점이에요. 세션 상태가 Driver 메모리에 남아 있어서, 새 서버가 준비됐다고 기존 서버를 바로 내릴 수는 없습니다. 그래서 서버를 준비하는 시점과 신규 세션을 전환하는 시점, 기존 서버를 종료하는 시점을 나눴어요. 새 generation의 서버를 모두 준비한 뒤 신규 세션의 목적지를 전환하는 Blue-Green 방식을 사용했어요. 기존 세션의 요청은 계속 원래 Driver로 보내고, 기존 서버는 세션 종료를 기다리는 drain 과정을 거쳐 정리합니다. 교체 전후의 서버 집합은 generation으로 구분합니다. attempt는 같은 Application의 실행 시도를 구분하는 값이에요. Application이 재시작돼도 generation은 그대로이고, 새 generation을 만들면 새로운 Application들이 각자의 생명주기를 시작해요. 새 서버가 모두 준비될 때까지 설정이 바뀌면 Tenant Operator는 새 generation을 만들어요. 기존 서버는 계속 요청을 처리하고, 새 서버가 목표 수만큼 모두 준비돼 일정 시간 안정적으로 유지되면 전환합니다. 새 서버가 제한 시간 안에 준비되지 않으면 교체를 취소하고 기존 서버를 유지해요. 마지막 성공 설정이 남아 있으면 그 설정으로 되돌려 같은 실패가 반복되지 않도록 합니다. 신규 세션의 목적지만 전환하기 Tenant Operator가 currentGeneration 을 변경하면 Gateway는 신규 세션을 새 generation으로 보내요. 기존 서버는 신규 세션을 받지 않는 drain 상태로 남아 원래 세션의 요청을 처리합니다. 전환이 끝나도 기존 서버는 남아 있어요 기존 서버는 남은 세션이 모두 종료되면 삭제해요. 세션 수를 확인할 수 없으면 기다리지만, drain 시작 후 기본 90분이 지나면 서버를 삭제하므로 남아 있는 세션은 끊길 수 있습니다. 업데이트는 신규 세션의 목적지를 새 서버로 전환하면 완료돼요. 기존 서버 정리는 별도로 진행하므로 오래 유지되는 세션이 다음 설정 변경을 막지는 않습니다. Spark Connect 서버는 언제부터 요청을 받을 수 있을까? 새 서버로 전환하려면 실제로 Connect 요청을 받을 준비가 됐는지 확인해야 해요. Driver가 Ready면 새 세션을 받아도 될까 Apache Spark Operator의 DriverReady 는 Driver Pod의 Ready 조건을 읽은 결과예요. 저희는 이를 새 서버로 전환하는 기준으로 사용하므로, readiness probe가 Connect 서버의 연결 준비 상태를 확인하도록 구성해야 했어요. 처음 시도한 Spark UI의 /connect/json HTTP probe에는 문제가 있었어요. Connect 서버가 뜨기 전에도 해당 경로가 다른 페이지로 리다이렉트됐고, 이 응답이 probe 성공으로 처리됐습니다. UI만 뜬 상태에서 Driver가 Ready로 표시될 수 있었던 거죠. 그래서 Connect 포트에 gRPC 연결을 시도하고 최대 3초 안에 연결이 성립하는지 확인하는 exec probe로 바꿨어요. Spark Tenant Operator가 이 probe를 Driver Pod 템플릿에 넣습니다. 실제 세션이나 쿼리를 실행하지는 않으므로 Executor 용량까지 보장하지는 않아요. Executor 연결과 Driver Ready가 서로를 기다린다면 Connect 포트를 readiness 기준으로 삼자 Spark의 기동 순서와 맞물리는 문제가 드러났어요. title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.

title: Language Is a Security Surface for Agent Guards
abstract: Step-level guards decide, before each tool call, whether an agent's next action is safe given the user's request and the trajectory so far. Users write those requests in many languages, while guard prompts and the benchmarks on which purpose-built guards are trained and evaluated are English. We ask whether a guard's verdict depends on the language of the request. We build LinguaGuardBench from the 1,220 labelled steps of TS-Bench AgentDojo-Traj: we translate only the user instruction into German, French, Turkish, Swahili and Amharic, and keep every tool call, observation and label byte-identical, so any change in a verdict is attributable to language alone. Six English rewordings and a whitespace placebo serve as controls, and managed guards are run three times to measure their noise. Across 19 guards, from frontier APIs to 4B open models and four purpose-built agent guards, most open, small and purpose-built guards change verdicts under translation beyond their own noise floor, and the effect grows with the rarity of the language: among the nine guards below 13B parameters, the mean placebo-adjusted flip rate rises from +1.5 pp on French to +4.4 pp on Amharic. Purpose-built guards are the most sensitive. The direction of the damage tends to follow guard size: open guards of 12-30B parameters block more benign steps (up to +5.0 pp false positives), and every significant loss of recall is in a guard below 10B (up to -7.4 pp). Frontier guards shift by at most about one point; the strongest, Gemini 3.8 Flash, returns identical verdicts with and without the request. The damage is concentrated in a few instructions and, in a post-hoc analysis, falls on steps where the agent's reasoning restates the English request, consistent with guards reacting to inconsistency between channels. English paraphrase moves every guard less than translation does. We release the benchmark and all 489k verdicts.

title: Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations
abstract: AI agents take actions through tools. Some actions are sensitive, so guards that supervise them must themselves be evaluated reliably. Yet the data used to evaluate a guard can include cues that make labels predictable without measuring the intended safety construct, and those cues can also influence guard decisions. We introduce a three-level shortcut-auditing framework and audit completed LinuxArena trajectories and two TS-Bench-derived step datasets. We distinguish label predictability, observational guard association, and paired decision sensitivity. In LinuxArena, shorter average shell commands strongly predict trajectory labels. In AgentDojo-Traj, exact-tool lookup falls from F_1=.901 with mixed-domain folds to .495 under domain holdout. In AgentHarm-Traj, released TS-Guard F_1 falls from .902 under row weighting to .719 with equal interaction weighting, while balanced accuracy rises. We then test the strongest safe-row marker association in a seven-configuration screen on a frozen 64-step AgentDojo-Traj cohort using repeated, interleaved Haiku calls. Rewriting the marker lowers blocking by 8.33 percentage points, while opaque tool aliases raise it by 11.46 points. All unsafe calls remain blocked; the changes concern false positives against inherited labels. Both effects remain nonzero after subtracting the formatting-placebo effect, with exploratory 95% ranges excluding zero. The same edits also change measured accuracy against inherited labels. This provides direct evidence that benchmark representation can materially change a guard's decisions and measured evaluation performance. The Haiku-sized effects do not reproduce in Luna or deterministic Q8 TS-Guard. We recommend domain group holdouts, evaluation-unit metrics, and placebo-controlled paired interventions.

title: How Much Physics Can Vision Learn from Audio? Probing and Distilling Damping Structure
abstract: Physical understanding is crucial for decision making, yet vision models struggle to infer properties such as damping that govern how materials behave. Audio encodes such properties directly, because an object's acoustic response to impact reveals its damping through measurable decay. We probe frozen encoders for the quality factor $Q$, a dimensionless measure of how many oscillations an object completes before its ring dies away, and report how well each embedding orders impacts by $Q$ using the Spearman rank correlation $ρ$, for which $ρ=1$ is a perfect ordering and $ρ=0$ an unrelated one. Audio embeddings reach $ρ=0.73$ and retain most of that advantage on materials withheld from training, while a single video frame taken at the moment of impact, encoded by CLIP, supports only $ρ=0.28$. Having established where the signal lives, we ask how much of that gap vision can recover. We distill a frozen audio teacher into a frozen CLIP backbone through a trained projection head and find that this recovers a useful fraction of the audio advantage. Because pooled correlations on this task are dominated in practice by category identity, we also evaluate under a leave-one-material-out protocol in which the held-out material is withheld from the projection head as well as the probe. Distillation with a four-frame input improves the correlation there from 0.234 to 0.338 (+0.053 over the matched four-frame baseline, 14 of 17 materials), a gain that no category-level strategy can produce. Widening the visual input to four frames spanning the impact supplies half of that improvement at no acoustic cost, which indicates that part of what a single frame misses is visible dynamics.

title: DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction
abstract: Key-value (KV) cache management has become a critical bottleneck for scaling Large Language Models (LLMs) to long-context scenarios due to linear memory growth. While recent eviction methods have moved beyond simple attention-score heuristics to incorporate value representations, they typically face a fundamental trade-off: the underlying optimization for minimizing output perturbation is an NP-hard combinatorial problem, leading to mathematically suboptimal heuristics or implementations that are difficult to kernelize. In this work, we propose DropKV, a simple principled eviction framework based on Decoupled Residual-Output Perturbation. By decoupling the joint eviction decision into independent per-token scoring, DropKV circumvents combinatorial intractability and admits a provable constant-factor approximation guarantee under a cone condition that we empirically verify on three long-context LLMs. To ensure practical viability, we provide a high-performance implementation using fused Triton kernels that avoid materializing the full attention matrix, delivering a 19.8x scoring-kernel speedup that translates to up to a 9.9% matched-batch end-to-end prefill speedup. Extensive evaluations on the RULER and LongBench benchmarks demonstrate that DropKV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines at equivalent cache budgets, achieving the lowest inference latency among eviction methods while also remaining faster than the dynamic cache baseline.

title: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
abstract: Modern agentic systems extend language models with external tools, enabling them to complete complex tasks through multi-turn interactions. As these agents are deployed in consequential settings, they are often constrained by policies governing pricing, privacy, confirmation, safety, and other requirements. However, existing evaluation methods leave a critical gap: capability benchmarks measure what agents can accomplish, while content-safety red-teaming measures harmful generations, but neither tests whether agents comply with predefined policies during otherwise valid tool use. Such policy violations are difficult to audit because their effects may emerge only after several turns, span multiple tool calls, or surface in downstream systems. We propose PROBE (Policy Rule Observation via Behavioral Exploration), an algorithm for training LLM-based auditors that interact with deployed agents as realistic users and probe them for policy violations through multi-turn, tool-mediated dialogue. We formalize agent auditing as a two-player Markov game and propose a composite reward that balances violation discovery, behavioral plausibility, conversation progress, and policy diversity. To study training objectives and reward design, we compare GRPO, DPO, and GFlowNet-based optimization in a controlled setting. Across extensive experiments, auditors trained with PROBE uncover substantially broader and higher-yield policy violations than same-architecture zero-shot adversaries, even when the auditor is significantly smaller than the target agent. Our results show that multi-turn behavioral auditing is a distinct and necessary axis of agent evaluation, complementing capability and safety benchmarks. PROBE offers a scalable path toward automated policy auditing for real-world agentic systems and suggests a co-evolutionary loop in which auditors expose failures and agents improve from auditor feedback.

title: Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models
abstract: Traditional reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms face significant limitations in handling long-term tasks with sparse rewards. Recent advancements have leveraged large language models (LLMs) to enhance RL by utilizing their world knowledge for task planning and reward generation. However, planning-based approaches often depend on pre-defined skill libraries and fail to optimize low-level control policies, while reward-based methods require extensive human feedback or exhaustive searching due to the complexity of tasks. In this paper, we propose the Progress Reward Model for RL (PRM4RL), a novel framework that integrates task planning and dense reward to enhance RL. For high-level planning, a complex task is decomposed into a series of simple manageable subtasks, with a subtask-oriented, fine-grained progress function designed to monitor task execution progress. For low-level reward generation, inspired by potential-based reward shaping, we use the progress function to construct a Progress Reward Model (PRM), providing theoretically grounded optimality and convergence guarantees, thereby enabling effective policy optimization. Experimental results on robotics control tasks demonstrate that our approach outperforms both LLM-based planning and reward methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance. Code is available at https://github.com/deng-ai-lab/PRM4RL.

title: Effectiveness of Hidden-State Probes for Localizing Reasoning Failures
abstract: Verifying the final answer of a long reasoning trace may show that the trace is wrong but it does not distinguish three cases. The problem may lie beyond the model's capability, another attempt would succeed, or one step in an otherwise recoverable trace made the trace fail. Standard hidden-state probes are trained on final-answer correctness, a label that conflates these cases. Monte Carlo rollouts distinguish the cases and locate the failing step at additional inference cost. We test the hidden states of 4B and 8B reasoning models for the failure type and the failing step and compare each probe with the strongest baseline that uses no hidden states. On incorrect 8B traces, the confidence probe, a calibrated correctness probe at a midpoint cutoff, misses 81% of cases in which a single step makes the trace unrecoverable and 47% of cases in which another attempt would succeed. A probe with a different training design over the same states reverses the ordering of these two kinds of failure, so either ordering can be read from those states. At both scales, no single tested probe locates the failing step more accurately than a rule based only on trace length, and at 4B a probe trained to predict that step fails to outperform this rule in any of 10 runs on identical traces. The confidence probe therefore indicates that an answer is wrong, but its failure-type ordering depends on its training design.

title: Learning Lean Feedback for Efficient Proof-Candidate Evaluation on GPUs
abstract: Training language models for formal theorem proving requires large numbers of verifier calls. Slow checks and timeouts often leave GPUs waiting and withhold rewards from potentially correct proofs. We train neural evaluators to predict Lean 4 verdicts and compiler feedback on GPUs using 4.84M labelled programs. We compare two validity classifiers with a feedback model that annotates proof attempts with predicted goal states and error messages. A two-stage evaluator that screens candidates with a classifier and scores its positive predictions with the feedback model reaches 87.8% accuracy in predicting whether Lean accepts a candidate proof, evaluated on a 68,932-program benchmark collected from public provers. The combined evaluator processes 3.5 candidates per second on one H100, 4.2x the throughput of our 64-worker Lean baseline with environment reuse. Finally, we combine our evaluator with Lean verdicts to obtain a hybrid reward system that shortens GRPO training steps by approximately 31%. After one GRPO epoch with hybrid rewards, the prover achieves nearly the same miniF2F pass@1 as with Lean-only rewards (62.2% versus 62.4%) and a pass@32 of 72.4% versus 71.3%.

title: Lethe: Link Inference Attacks For Evaluation of Edge Unlearning Methods
abstract: Graph Unlearning (GU) aims to remove the influence of specific training data from a Graph Neural Network without retraining anew. While most methods address removal of nodes and features, Edge Unlearning (EU), aiming at forgetting edges, has recently attracted dedicated attention as a standalone problem due to the hardness of completely removing the impact of an edge in the model. Despite this, no dedicated benchmark for EU exists besides isolated evaluations on feature-rich datasets such as Cora and Citeseer where GNNs exploit node features rather than graph structure. As such, we show two systematic limitations in existing evaluations: dedicated EU methods can be slower than retraining anew, and accuracy metrics are uninformative due to the negligible impact of edge removal. To address this gap, we introduce Lethe, the first comprehensive benchmark for Edge Unlearning, featuring 15 methods and 8 datasets. Our benchmark emphasizes large graphs, introduces evaluation tasks of varying difficulty, and proposes empirical measures based on link inference attacks rather than proxy accuracy metrics. We provide a comprehensive empirical analysis, demonstrate the shortcomings of current evaluations, and release Lethe as a reproducible, extensible benchmark.

title: Pairwise AUC Optimization Needs Corrective Power: A Unified View
abstract: Direct pairwise AUC-surrogate training is attractive because it trains toward the ranking metric used at test time, especially under class imbalance. This creates a direct alignment between the training objective and the evaluation metric, but such metric alignment alone does not guarantee that stochastic training remains corrective. We study this gap through Corrective Power: whether pairwise mini-batch updates produce stronger and more reliable improvements for more severe positive-negative ranking errors. Our main observation is that direct pairwise training can enter regions where severe errors remain common but no longer produce useful corrective motion. In such regions, even the mini-batch noise that would normally help SGD move along the steepest severe-error correction direction can become much weaker. In this paper, we seek a theoretical explanation for this by exploring the degenerate property of the U-statistics formed from the pairwise gradients therein. Our results provide a mechanistic explanation for several empirical patterns: (a) squared-hinge loss is often an effective AUC surrogate; (b) cross-entropy warm-up can help models that enter the AUC phase from a poor starting region; and (c) parameter-efficient fine-tuning from a pretrained model can reduce that need by starting closer to a favorable ranking geometry. Experiments on 8 CV tasks and 8 NLP tasks, using ResNet50, DenseNet121, DistilBERT-base, and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, support these predictions.

title: Market Incentives for AI Safety Investment
abstract: Despite their practical significance, modern AI systems pose significant societal risks, including toxicity, malicious use, and misinformation. Their mitigation depends not only on technical feasibility but also on the incentives of firms that develop and deploy these systems. We show how profit maximization shapes safety investment in an AI supply chain with an upstream LLM provider and several competing downstream firms. In our game-theoretic model, we derive the market-driven level of safety investment and compare it with the levels that maximize market welfare and industry profit. We find that downstream competition generally induces downstream firms to invest more in safety than the industry-profit-optimal level. By contrast, the upstream provider may underinvest relative to these benchmarks because it is not fully compensated for the surplus from safety investments. Finally, we analyze how different regulatory interventions affect the participants' incentives and profits, and the resulting levels of model safety.

title: ClaimScope: Label-Blind Witness Verification for Mathematical Claim Auditing
abstract: Mathematical agents are commonly evaluated by answer accuracy or proof acceptance. We introduce ClaimScope, a 72-task benchmark for auditing proposed claims through a verdict, scope, counterexample, and repair. Tasks cover optimizer-state transport, finite-horizon affine recurrences, and exact $2\times2$ linear algebra. We evaluate Qwen3-8B with direct generation and four matched two-pass conditions, each starting from the same draft. A witness checker evaluates only the model's submitted state, without consulting reference verdicts or supplying a replacement witness. Its feedback still conveys information about validity: a verified refutation establishes that the claim is false, and rejection reasons can suggest structural fixes. In this evaluation, verifier feedback yields $23/39$ accepted counterexamples on invalid claims and $25/72$ safe completions, compared with $15/39$ and $20/72$ for checker-free generic feedback. Strict completion remains $17/72$; verdict accuracy changes from $47/72$ to $46/72$. The claim-grouped safe-completion difference is $.094$, with a bootstrap 95\% interval of $[.000,.198]$. All seven task-level gains follow horizon/input-length diagnostics. A post-hoc schema-only correction of the direct outputs reaches the same 25 safe tasks without another model call. These results separate claim classification from executable evidence, while locating the observed gains in witness-structure correction rather than demonstrating broader reasoning improvement.

title: BiShield-TEE: On the (In-)Security of Unilateral Weight Obfuscation in On-Device TEE-Shielded LLM Partition
abstract: On-device deployment of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly adopted due to latency and privacy requirements, but exposes proprietary models to reverse engineering and intellectual property theft. Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) provide hardware-enforced isolation for on-device inference, yet most TEE-based parameter obfuscation relies on unilateral matrix transformations that obfuscate only output side. We identify a vulnerability in this design, termed the \emph{Solution Determinacy Property (SDP)}: the obfuscation secret is uniquely determined, exposing the structure of the true key and enabling attackers to break the protection. Under our attacks, representative methods \textsc{GroupCover} and \textsc{ArrowCloak} are reduced to negligible protection, with attack accuracy reaching over $2.4\times$ the full-shielding black-box baseline and recovering near-complete model functionality.To address this vulnerability, we propose \textsc{BiShield-TEE}, a bilateral framework that induces \emph{Ambiguous Solutions} through joint obfuscation of input and output dimensions, hiding the true key among many equally valid candidates. Experiments across diverse models and datasets show that \textsc{BiShield-TEE} confines attack accuracy to the full-shielding black-box baseline, while achieving higher inference efficiency than prior methods on real hardware.Our code is available at https://github.com/laduiw/BiShield-TEE.

title: When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark
abstract: Muon's gains in data efficiency motivate evaluating its performance under explicit data, time, and tuning budgets. On a single A100 GPU, we compare a reference single-device Muon implementation with AdamW across 17.7M- and 33.6M-parameter causal language models and 2.70M-parameter vision transformers. A common 23-candidate development budget selects configurations evaluated with five matched seeds, full validation trajectories, optimizer-step timing, and a frozen one-shot test. Muon reduces validation-loss area under the curve by 3.25--22.44\% at equal data and lowers test loss in all 20 primary pairs. In this configuration, Muon improves time-normalized loss area} by 19.68--22.31\% on vision, while AdamW is better by 3.38--6.96\% on language. The full Muon optimizer call, including auxiliary AdamW updates, consumes 56.1--69.6\% of training time, compared with 6.1--9.1\% for the AdamW baseline. Muon also has higher expected regret under restricted access to these candidate pools. These results characterize small models with reference kernels; their wall-clock ordering does not establish a ranking for larger models or optimized implementations.

title: Poison Valleys: Diagnosing Path-Dependent Failure in LLM Code Repair
abstract: When code-repair agents fail, final tests reveal that a patch is wrong but not which earlier commitment caused it or which software obligation failed. Poison Valleys traces this path in 1,844 model requests on two synthetic Python cases: PersistQueue adds atomic batch claiming to a disk-backed queue, while Dijkstra adds source-sensitive filtering to shortest-path search. We define plausible but incorrect software mechanisms, place each in a model's hypothesis, implementation plan, or both, and evaluate the generated code with an Oracle and targeted diagnostic coordinates. Moving the misconception from hypothesis to plan increased failure by 32.2% in PersistQueue and 28.9% in Dijkstra after matching the experimental mix. Different misconceptions produced distinct, model-dependent patterns of violated obligations, although several could converge on the same behavior. This creates a measured connection from upstream misconception to code mechanism and failure form. Code, data, and demo: https://poisonvalleys.org.

title: Does Compression Imply Generalization? A Minimum Description Length Perspective
abstract: A central question in modern learning theory is what notion of compression, if any, explains why over-parameterized neural networks generalize. Existing answers measure complexity at different levels, ranging from weights to representations; however, estimating the associated quantities either requires held-out data in principle or relies on the challenging (ultra) high-dimensional mutual information estimation. To overcome these challenges, we approach the question through the minimum description length (MDL) principle, and specifically, we propose the prequential regret as a complementary signal that is computable from the training trajectory alone. We establish that, in the (nearly) interpolating regime, the expected prequential regret upper-bounds the description length of the trained parameter under the algorithm-induced distribution, and that this description length translates into a high-probability generalization bound in the PAC-MDL setting. Along the way, we show that the encoder-complexity correction recently added to the algorithm-level information bottleneck (IB) is upper-bounded by an MDL parameter description length, \new{bringing together} the two views of compression from MDL and IB. Empirically, the prequential regret tracks the generalization error on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, with Pearson correlations exceeding 0.9.

title: Rethinking Learning from Label Proportions via Moment Matching
abstract: Learning from label proportions (LLP) is a weakly supervised setting where training data are grouped into bags with only bag-level label proportions observed, and the goal is to learn a classifier that predicts labels for individual instances. Recently, a large body of methods has emerged; however, most of them rely on the assumption that instance-label pairs are sampled i.i.d. and randomly assembled into bags, an assumption often violated in real-world scenarios. Our experimental results indicate that these methods perform suboptimally under non-random settings. In this work, we adopt a more realistic assumption: bags are sampled i.i.d., and instance labels are conditionally independent given the instances. Under this setting, we show that the label counts follow a Poisson multinomial distribution. Motivated by this observation, we propose LLP via moment matching (LLP-MM), a simple yet effective approach which leverages multi-order factorial moments as training objectives, encouraging the classifier predictions to match these moments and thereby more fully exploit the underlying statistical structure of the data. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets under various bag construction strategies demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach while maintaining high computational efficiency. Our code is available at https://github.com/TianhaoMa5/LLP-MM.

title: Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demand efficient inference, where the multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations in linear projections dominate compute and energy cost. Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces this cost by mapping weights and activations to low-bit integers. Power-of-Two (PoT) weight quantization promises efficient multiplier-free LLM inference via shift-add logic, but suffers significant accuracy degradation at low bitwidths due to its coarse base-2 quantization grid. We introduce Fractional PoT (FPoT), a base-$\sqrt{2}$ (half-octave) fractional PoT grid that achieves practical 4-bit weight quantization while preserving a fully integer shift-add datapath. The method combines (i) the base-$\sqrt{2}$ weight grid with uniform integer activations, (ii) a calibration-time grid-alignment refinement absorbed into the static per-channel scale, and (iii) a lightweight 1-adder $\sqrt{2}$ approximation whose error is absorbed during weight calibration via approximate-grid quantization, yielding a processing element (PE) with significantly fewer gates than a 4-bit integer multiplier. On Llama-3-8B with 4-bit weight and activation quantization, FPoT improves zero-shot commonsense reasoning performance by 8.72% relative to the PoT baseline, while maintaining performance close to the uniform integer baseline, with only a negligible 0.4%p degradation. These results hold across various configurations spanning seven models and three bit-widths. Furthermore, FPoT can be integrated with state-of-the-art LLM PTQ methods, demonstrating framework-agnostic applicability.

title: RecSoup: Efficient Model Merging Approach for Controllable Multi-Objective Recommendation
abstract: Recommender systems often need to balance multiple conflicting objectives. Controllable Multi-Objective Recommendation (CMOR) enables dynamic adjustment of objective trade-offs at inference time without retraining, adapting to shifting user or system requirements. Existing CMOR approaches typically rely on output-level reranking or parameter-generating modules, which either limit the scope of feasible trade-offs or incur substantial training and inference cost. Model merging provides a promising alternative by reusing multiple objective-specific models via parameter combination. However, its direct application to recommender systems is challenging due to the lack of a shared linear regime and cross-objective interference. To address these issues, we propose RecSoup, a lightweight two-stage approach for effective CMOR via specialized model merging. RecSoup first mitigates parameter interference across objectives through a pruning strategy that jointly considers objective-specific importance and cross-objective relevance. It then performs adaptive parameter merging via a learnable preference-to-coefficient mapping, allowing dynamic trade-off control at inference time without joint retraining or additional generative modules. Theoretically, we prove that RecSoup outperforms the parameter generation paradigm in effectiveness and efficiency, as it can fully navigate the Pareto front without smoothness constraints. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that RecSoup achieves improved Pareto front quality and effective controllability while delivers 165--228x faster inference-time latency than parameter generation approaches. Code is available at https://github.com/35798642/RECSOUP.git.

title: Clean Data Can Still Carry Backdoors: Support-Persistent Backdoors for Model Reuse
abstract: Traditional backdoor attacks inject artificial trigger patterns into training data, causing models to misclassify triggered inputs while maintaining normal behavior on clean samples. Since these artificial triggers are absent in clean datasets, standard knowledge distillation (KD) typically eliminates them, leading to the common belief that KD serves as an effective purification defense. In this paper, we propose DAR (Discover-and-Relabel), a support-persistent backdoor method that retains its behavior even after clean-data distillation. DAR identifies naturally abundant patterns in low-dimensional feature subspaces using subspace clustering and applies label-only poisoning to samples that inherently satisfy the discovered rule. At test time, the backdoor is activated by locally modifying the corresponding subspace of the target images. By instantiating spatial and frequency operators, DAR achieves attack accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art backdoor attacks in ImageNet classification and CLIP-based prompt tuning. Notably, DAR keeps attack success above 96% after clean KD and remains defense-resistant in practice. Project page: https://junhoo.me/backdoor

title: Sensor Diagnosis for Fuel and Emissions Monitoring in Heavy-Duty Diesel Vehicles
abstract: Faulty sensor readings can distort estimates of fuel use and carbon dioxide emissions from diesel engines. We evaluate two procedures that use relationships learned from healthy measurements to diagnose faults and guide fuel correction. The diagnosis procedure tests whether replacing a suspected faulty reading with an estimated healthy value helps a model predict another sensor's recorded reading more accurately. It then predicts the fault type and decides whether to report the diagnosis. We evaluate five synthetic fault types on 217 steady-state operating points from a heavy-duty diesel engine, excluding all measurements at selected engine speeds from training. Across 31,500 fault-injected groups of 20 operating points, it issues diagnoses for 77.3% of groups, with 92.1% of diagnoses issued on these groups correct. The fuel correction procedure uses a different sensor-selection rule at individual operating points, testing how each replacement changes the largest prediction error across all six sensors. Fuel correction requires a fault alarm and engine speed and torque close to the training conditions. A fuel reading is replaced only when its replacement reduces the largest prediction error sufficiently more than replacements for the other sensors. Assuming faults in 1% of one-hour scenarios, equally likely sensors and fault types, and equal time at each measured condition, selected fuel corrections reduce mean absolute error in calculated combustion CO2 by 83.8%. On this engine map, learned relationships support complete sensor diagnoses and fuel corrections that improve emissions accounting while preserving unaffected readings.

title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation
abstract: Post-hoc image explanations usually show where a model looks using spatial heatmaps or indicate which channels matter using global channel scores. These separate views are limiting for multispectral data because channel relevance is often spatially localized and physically meaningful. We introduce Spectral-Spatial Interpretation (SSI), a full-grid attribution method over position-channel players (g,c). For each spatial position, SSI fixes the observed surrounding context, defines a conditional game over the channels at that position, and applies the Shapley value to this local game. The result is a full spectral-spatial attribution matrix rather than a single heatmap or a global channel ranking. SSI has a clear local interpretation. It satisfies Shapley fairness within each position, and aggregating its channel attributions exactly recovers the position-level contextual contrast obtained by replacing that position with the baseline. SSI also differs from context-averaged Owen-style hierarchical accounting, which uses the same position-channel grouping but averages over external spatial coalitions. On HLS Burn Scar, SSI outperforms an MC-Owen estimator across retained attribution metrics while using only about 6% of its evaluation budget. Across CUB-200, EuroSAT, and HLS Burn Scar under both per-channel mean and zero baselines, SSI achieves the best joint deletion and insertion AUC over dense, flat, and rank-1 baselines, yields the strongest spectral hit rates and channel deletion, and leads spatial localization on both annotated datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/AtheavenMa/Spectral-Spatial-Interpretation.

title: SIEVE: Overcoming Topological Obstruction in Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: We identify a theoretical incompatibility between 3D point cloud masked autoencoding and SE(3)-equivariant networks. We prove that standard masking triggers a topological collapse, effectively forcing the model to hallucinate orientation without a reference frame. To resolve this, we introduce SIEVE (Scalar Invariant Extraction Via Equivariance), an SE(3)-equivariant self-supervised framework that compresses point cloud geometry into invariant scalar embeddings. At its core is the spherical projection mask, which preserves global pose while obfuscating local semantics, sidestepping the obstruction by construction. Experiments confirm that SIEVE circumvents the predicted collapse where constant and noise masks fail. On downstream point cloud tasks, the resulting embeddings improve over coordinate-based baselines and hand-crafted geometric descriptors, with the largest gains on generalization to unseen shape categories.

title: StochLOB: Heavy-Tailed Score Matching for Robust Limit Order Book Trend Prediction
abstract: Score-based diffusion methods usually perturb data with Brownian Gaussian noise, corresponding to a light-tailed forward stochastic differential equation (SDE). For market time series this SDE can be a poor abstraction: limit order book (LOB) order flow is heavy-tailed, bursty, and occasionally jump-like. We study STOCHLOB, a training-only score-matching framework that changes the forward diffusion corruption law while leaving the deployed predictor deterministic. Instead of Brownian-only Gaussian corruption, the noising process uses two non-Gaussian SDE-inspired alternatives: jump-Lévy noise through a compound-Poisson variance mixture, and clipped $α$-stable noise through a positive-stable Gaussian scale mixture. These corruptions inject finite jumps and heavy-tailed residuals into training without requiring reverse-time diffusion sampling at inference. The resulting score target has a useful interpretation: its radial factor $h_t(r)$ is the posterior expected corruption precision, so large residuals are weighted according to the latent corruption scale that most plausibly generated them. On chronologically held-out Coinbase LOB data, the proposed variants remain competitive on uncorrupted BTC and altcoin test horizons and improve several realized tail-window stress diagnostics. An exploratory Feishu A-share transfer study further tests whether the probability outputs remain usable under transaction costs and trading-rule constraints. Code and configuration files are available at https://github.com/ArshiAbolghasemi/Penny.

title: On the Last-Iterate Convergence of Clipped Gradient Methods
abstract: In stochastic (strongly) convex optimization, establishing last-iterate convergence guarantees for first-order methods has recently garnered increasing attention, as this not only deepens the theoretical understanding of these algorithms but also aligns more closely with practice. Notably, people have demonstrated that one of the most famous, simple, and popular methods, Stochastic Gradient Descent ($\mathtt{SGD}$), provably achieves last-iterate convergence. However, the existing results may have limited applicability, since they typically rely on strong conditions on the gradient noise (e.g., an exponentially decaying tail) rather than the more realistic heavy-tailed noise. Unfortunately, when faced with heavy-tailed noise, $\mathtt{SGD}$ is known to exhibit undesirable behavior or even fail to converge. To address the challenge of heavy-tailed noise, people have proposed $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$, an algorithm that combines $\mathtt{SGD}$ with a simple mechanism, gradient clipping. Although $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$ performs well in practice, its last-iterate convergence property remains highly underexplored. In this work, we prove the first optimal last-iterate rates in high probability for $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$ under heavy-tailed noise, thereby closing a gap in the literature.

title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
abstract: When does a language model acquire a capability? Developmental studies usually answer this by tracking when models start producing the correct token. But that prediction passes through the unembedding matrix, or readout, which is itself still being learned during pretraining. We show that a model's hidden states can encode task information before its own readout expresses it, so timelines read from outputs conflate what the model encodes with what its readout expresses. To track the readout directly, we introduce parameter-trajectory crosscoding, which fits one sparse dictionary to every token's readout row at every checkpoint. Unlike crosscoders on activations, it needs only checkpoint weights. We use it to locate a narrow early window, 0.4-1.1% of the way through Pythia's pretraining, in which the readout reorganizes and WordNet word categories become decodable from its rows. By then, linear probes on the hidden states already decode task information that the model's own outputs do not yet show. To test whether such gaps depend on how fast the readout learns, we pretrain small models from scratch that differ only in the readout's learning rate. We find that raising it makes the readout develop earlier and the gap close sooner, with little effect on final loss. Together, these results imply that early in training, where many developmental transitions are dated, a behavioral date can reflect when the readout learns to express task information and not when the model learns it.

title: CausalEvo: Causal Skill Self-Evolution for Health LLM Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents for health can accumulate reusable textual skills from task feedback, such as calculation criteria, measurement time points, and formula units. Deciding which skills to retain is consequential: useful rules improve later answers, while faulty generalizations propagate errors. We propose CausalEvo, a method for causal skill self-evolution that estimates the relative effects of deliberately changed skill sets while holding the model weights, feedback cases, and rule count fixed. At each evolution step, a frozen LLM proposes candidate rules, which are pooled with the incumbent skills so that the current skill set remains a feasible choice. Paired skill replacements against shared background rules are scored on the same feedback cases; least squares converts the score differences into relative skill values, and the top-ranked rules are retained, favoring incumbents on ties. A decision-loss bound separates candidate support, approximation, and estimation errors. On six MedCalc-Bench-Verified tasks with 120 held-out cases, CausalEvo achieves 60.00% accuracy, compared with 55.83% for SkillOpt and 51.67% without skills. Across the recorded training configurations, which use different optimization budgets, it consumes 55.6% fewer training tokens than SkillOpt. Gains concentrate in particular calculations alongside regressions on others, and paired accuracy intervals include zero. CausalEvo turns task feedback into controlled decisions about skill retention and replacement. Project repository: https://github.com/txbrook/CausalEvo

title: MSP: Modality Self-Play for Training Multimodal LLMs Without Paired Cross-Modal Data
abstract: Large multimodal models have achieved remarkable progress by scaling model capacity and training on massive paired multimodal data. However, this paradigm introduces a fundamental bottleneck: aligned multimodal datasets are expensive to curate, difficult to scale across diverse modality combinations, and increasingly constrain further progress. We introduce Modality Self-Play (MSP), a training framework for multimodal foundation models based on proxy-mediated modality composition. Instead of relying on paired cross-modal data, MSP uses anchor-supporting proxy textual descriptions of unseen modalities as semantic bridges during training. Given an observed modality (e.g., image or audio), the model generates proxy descriptions for complementary unseen modalities, which are then encoded and aligned with the observed modality through learned bridges, enabling cross-modal interaction without real paired non-text supervision. Our central hypothesis is that proxy text, combined with contrastively trained pretrained encoders, provides sufficient semantic structure for multimodal composition to emerge. We show that MSP enables zero-shot modality composition: models trained only with a real anchor modality and accompanying proxy descriptions can integrate and reason over multiple modalities at inference time despite never observing real paired non-text data during training. Empirically, MSP achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on multiple multimodal benchmarks. Ablation studies further demonstrate that learned bridges improve alignment, while anchor-supporting proxy descriptions enable effective cross-modal composition. MSP removes the need for real paired non-text (e.g., audio-vision) supervision, while continuing to rely on modality-text pairs, pretrained contrastive encoders, and modality-distribution bridge calibration.

title: Ranked Right, Sized Wrong: Ensemble Spread Fails Silently at Streamflow Extremes
abstract: Deep learning models, particularly Long Short-Term Memory networks, are increasingly used for operational streamflow forecasting, with ensemble spread providing a signal of predictive uncertainty. As climate change increases the frequency of hydroclimatic extremes, these models will increasingly operate under flow conditions that are rare in their historical records. We therefore evaluate whether ensemble spread remains informative under increasing flows, examining both its magnitude relative to error and its ability to rank errors. Prediction error is approximately $2\times$ the corrected spread at ordinary flows and up to $4\times$ at the highest flows, with the discrepancy increasing with flow (log-log slope $1.30$, 95% CI: $[1.20,1.41]$). Under-dispersion is strongest in observed extreme flows beyond the training record, reaching an $18\times$ discrepancy. This is pervasive and not explainable by conditional mean bias. Area Under the Sparsification Error, a standard distribution-free metric of uncertainty ranking, describing how well a model knows when it is uncertain, indicates near-oracle ranking for ensemble spread ($0.071$), yet ordering by predicted discharge alone nearly matches it. Informative uncertainty ranking can coexist with severe under-dispersion. In deployment, error ranking cannot be verified, yet the spread is available, and it is relied on as the uncertainty signal under increasingly extreme conditions, while systematically understating risk, most severely for the extreme events that matter most.

title: Pixels to Tokens: Token Space Efficient Active Learning for Low-Budget Semantic Segmentation
abstract: While foundation models and vision transformers (ViTs) have redefined visual representations, current active learning (AL) strategies for these backbones largely operate at the patch or region level, where annotation requirements remain high due to extensive pixel labeling. Extending ViT-based AL to the pixel-level, low-budget regime is uniquely challenging: with as little as one pixel query per image, a method must simultaneously identify the most informative locations and train a reliable decoder head from an extremely sparse signal. We introduce TEAL (Token-space Efficient Active Learning), the first pixel-level AL framework built around ViT representations. TEAL uses a frozen ViT backbone and performs diversity-based selection directly on its native token lattice, avoiding the artifacts introduced by interpolating token embeddings to dense pixel resolutions. Our framework applies a two-level MaxHerding strategy over multi-layer token descriptors to select representative candidates, followed by margin-based uncertainty refinement on a finer decoder grid. Across CamVid, Cityscapes, ADE20K, and Pascal Context, TEAL consistently outperforms previous baselines under extreme label scarcity, improving over the strongest baseline by up to +24.36 mIoU with a single labeled pixel (px) per image, and reaching up to 97% of fully supervised performance with just 10 px. To rigorously establish the source of the gains, we further show that the improvements persist when all baselines are equipped with the same DINOv3 backbone, demonstrating that coupling token-space selection with uncertainty refinement on the decoder grid makes ViT token geometry an effective foundation for extremely low-budget active segmentation.

title: Complete or Sparse: A Tale of Two Identifiabilities
abstract: Understanding when neural networks learn interpretable representations is central to mechanistic interpretability. We study this through identifiability: when can supervised learning recover the true latent variables underlying the data? We introduce two data generating processes distinguished by their causal direction where either labels cause latents (generative) or latents cause labels (discriminative). When the representation has at least as many dimensions as the latent space, we prove that the optimal encoders are linear in the latents. Conversely, when dimensions are insufficient, identifiability generically fails and encoders become nonlinear. We then show that additional constraints yield recovery of individual latent variables, not just linear mixtures. In the generative setting, non-negative activations and energy efficiency force each neuron to encode exactly one latent, providing a precise account of selective grandmother cell-like responses. In the discriminative setting, when latents are sparse and the true measurement matrix satisfies the spark condition, the learned encoder inherits compressed sensing structure, enabling sparse dictionary learning to perfectly recover individual latents. This constitutes, to our knowledge, the first identifiability result for undercomplete nonlinear independent component analysis. Our framework unifies nonlinear ICA, compressed sensing, and neural network interpretability, delineating exactly when representations transition from nonlinear distortions to linear representations and, under additional constraints or steps, to clean, axis-aligned codes. Theoretical predictions are validated on synthetic benchmarks and on activations drawn from vision models, large language models, and macaque inferotemporal cortex.

title: Confidence-Calibrated Inference Expansion for Evaluator-Guided Test-Time Reasoning
abstract: Evaluator-guided reasoning presents a local control problem at every step: trust the current answer, return a fallback, or spend more inference. We formulate this choice as a compute-aware three-action controller, scoring terminal actions by predicted answer success and expansion by a rollout-based continuation-success surrogate, with compute cost priced explicitly. A local action-gap analysis characterizes when score errors can change a decision, while an expected regret bound accounts for errors along the realized expansion path. Guided by this analysis, we learn and calibrate action-specific confidence estimates, with local uncertainty penalties for ambiguous decisions. On held-out width expansion and revision tasks, the controller improves observed utility over calibration-selected fixed policies while reducing normalized online compute by about 30% and 16%, respectively. Across four Qwen3-8B seeds, compute is lower than fitted Q in both settings, while utility differences are small and mixed. The results frame evaluator-guided reasoning as resource allocation under uncertainty, rather than a uniformly stronger reasoner.

title: What Does Disagreement Mean? A Semantic Identifiability Frontier for Pairwise Preference Learning
abstract: Pairwise comparison data are a standard supervision signal in preference learning, but disagreement in such data can reflect stable latent heterogeneity, ephemeral stochasticity, or non-binary responses hidden by a forced-choice interface. We study which of these semantic distinctions are identifiable from the feedback channel itself. We introduce a nonparametric latent semantic model with three querywise quantities: aggregate directional preference $μ_q$, persistent disagreement $τ_q$, and non-binary mass $α_q$. Under the anonymous binary channel, we prove an exact semantic fiber theorem: $μ_q$ is point-identified, whereas $(τ_q, α_q)$ vary over an explicit feasible region compatible with the same binary law. Same-annotator repeats identify $τ_q$ through a covariance identity, abstention-enabled feedback identifies $α_q$ directly, and together they point-identify the full semantic triple. We also derive finite-sample estimators, nonasymptotic concentration bounds, and semantics-aware action-recovery guarantees, and validate the theory on theorem-matched synthetic data.

title: Causal Syntax Circuits in CodeLMs: Budget and Probe Decide What Looks Localised
abstract: Code models write Python when the prompt does not say which language to use. We ask a mechanistic question about that habit: is it produced by a small, findable group of components inside the model? We run one pipeline---mean ablation, activation patching, greedy circuit extraction, a random-control significance test, and activation steering---over 55 model-language settings spanning ten open code models (five base and five instruction-tuned), three target languages (Rust, C#, PHP), two prompt suites, and two component budgets. We report five findings. First, the preference is large, grows with model size, and survives instruction tuning: it is larger on every instruction-tuned checkpoint than on its base version, by 12% on average. Second, its measured size is mostly a property of the probe; replacing our aligned prompts with XLCoST parallel functions takes the same measurement on the same models from about 1.6 to about 0.01. Third, whether the preference looks localised depends on how many components the search may keep: with a budget of 12, 1 of 15 settings yields a circuit that beats size-matched random controls after multiple-comparison correction, and with a budget of 40, 6 of 15 do. Fourth, interventions that a smaller-budget study reports as uniformly failing do sometimes succeed: patching makes a Python prompt prefer target syntax in 2 of 45 settings, and steering changes the most likely next token in 9 of 45. Fifth, every circuit whose effect is significant but points away from the target language comes from a setting where circuit extraction failed, which makes such results a diagnostic rather than a phenomenon. The practical lesson is that a claim about whether a behaviour is localised can turn on analysis choices that papers rarely report. We release the full grid so those choices can be varied.

title: The Accuracy Well: Nonmonotone Accuracy Dynamics at Vanishing Initialization
abstract: We study classification dynamics under small initialization and identify a pronounced non-monotone behavior of accuracy that we call the accuracy well: accuracy rises rapidly early in training, subsequently drops, and only much later recovers. We observe this phenomenon in deep linear networks, fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST, deep convolutional networks on CIFAR-10, and controlled synthetic tasks, across different losses and optimizers and in both training and test accuracy. We propose a three-stage explanation in terms of target-driven organization, a degeneracy bottleneck, and subsequent recruitment and recovery. We develop a rigorous theory of these dynamics for shallow and deep linear networks, showing in particular that high accuracy can emerge while the predictor and the change in loss remain asymptotically vanishing, before continued optimization causes accuracy to deteriorate. For a simple synthetic classification task, we prove an extreme instance in which accuracy asymptotically rises to 100%, collapses to 0, and later recovers permanently to 100%. Our results show that classification accuracy can reveal aspects of learning dynamics that are not captured by the training loss alone.

title: Fractional is Better: Learnable Derivative Orders in Neural Operator Learning
abstract: Neural operators learn mappings between function spaces, enabling fast surrogate solutions to partial differential equations. Despite remarkable architectural diversity, these methods often share a common input representation: raw coordinate-value pairs $(x, u(x))$. We ask whether inputs aligned with PDE differential structure can improve learning. Through Picard iteration on mild solutions, we show that derivatives of the input appear explicitly in the solution operator, suggesting that providing derivative features should reduce the network's implicit differentiation burden. We prove this intuition: providing derivative features improves approximation bounds from $O(W^{-(s-m)/d})$ to $O(W^{-s/d})$, where $W$ is parameter count, $s$ is input regularity, $m$ is the PDE order, and $d$ is spatial dimension. Our central finding, however, is a surprise: the optimal derivative order $β^*$ is strictly less than the PDE order $m$. This gap arises from a bias-variance tradeoff in spectral space that we characterize in closed form. Learning $β$ from data achieves automatic spectral regularization. We introduce $\partial$-NO (del-NO), for derivative-augmented neural operators, an architecture-agnostic augmentation that provides learnable fractional derivative features to any neural operator backbone. Across benchmark problems and architectures, $\partial$-NO consistently improves prediction accuracy, with learned orders that reflect a representation of known physics modulated by noise and finite-sample constraints.

title: Lifted State Policy Optimization: Internalizing Self-Correction through Transition Geometry
abstract: Preference optimization ranks final answers and trajectory RL maximizes aggregate returns, yet neither credits the local change that turns a flawed reasoning state into a better one. We introduce Lifted State Policy Optimization (LSPO), which establishes this finite, cost-adjusted transition as the primary unit of learning. Each textual answer is augmented with a learned continuous coordinate, forming a lifted state that an energy function evaluates and orders. A shaped reward drives energy descent net of edit and step costs, and an internalization loss absorbs selected low-energy answers into the direct generator. On Qwen3.5-27B, the resulting single-pass policy reaches 71.8% aggregate accuracy across mathematics, science, code, and logic benchmarks, matching test-time reflection at 71.9% with 28% lower latency and 25.8% fewer tokens. The pattern holds across dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, and matched controls confirm that transition credit and the lifted coordinate each contribute, as does answer internalization. Our code is available at https://github.com/Venomrko/lspo.

title: Read, Parse, Describe: Unified Document Parsing with Visual Element Description Generation
abstract: Document understanding systems are typically evaluated as separate components via layout analysis, optical text recognition, reading-order prediction, and image captioning. This separation leaves scientific figures, captions, and visual semantics weakly connected, and fails to measure whether a model can produce a single page-level parse that is both structurally faithful and semantically accessible. We introduce Read-Parse-Describe, a unified dataset for document parsing with visual element description generation. Given a page image, models are required to output an ordered list of layout elements containing bounding boxes, semantic labels, reading-order indices, recognized textual content, and alternative text descriptions for visual elements. The benchmark is built from 2,402 documents, comprising 18,163 continuous pages, 125,218 layout elements, and 11,338 visual instances. Besides, we further propose a plug-and-play space-awareness enhancer that reuses multi-layer visual features and injects grid-aware spatial guidance into vision-language tokens for layout-aware generation. Experiments across end-to-end VLMs and pipeline parsers show that existing systems still struggle to jointly recover reading order and visual semantics, while our enhanced model achieves strong joint performance. These results highlight the need to move beyond isolated document parsing modules toward unified models that jointly read, parse, and describe complex documents. The new dataset and code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yufanchen96/RPD

title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation For Robot Policies
abstract: Reinforcement-learning policies for robot locomotion can fail at deployment when operating conditions shift (e.g., rough or slippery terrain, payload changes, sensing degradation), and retraining or manual recalibration is often infeasible under on-device latency and memory constraints. We study test-time adaptation (TTA) for robotic control: adapting a pretrained policy online and in a self-supervised manner during execution, without access to rewards. Our starting point is a lightweight baseline that updates only the actor using a frozen pretrained critic as a deployment-time performance surrogate. Building on this, we introduce TEMPO, a test-time entropy-regularized, memory-guided policy optimization method that stabilizes critic-driven updates under severe shift. TEMPO combines (i) an entropy-promoting regularizer on the critic's predictive distribution to mitigate overconfident extrapolation, and (ii) a score-based memory, inspired by prioritized replay, that prioritizes low-value ("hard") observations and applies importance sampling to focus limited computation on the most informative deployment conditions. Across Go1, Go2, and G1 in MuJoCo Playground under four representative shifts and multiple architectures, TEMPO yields consistent gains, reaching up to 80% improvement in a single-device setting. We further validate on a physical Unitree Go2 with an added calf payload, where fully on-device adaptation improves performance over the non-adapted baseline across real-world episodes.

title: When Correctness Feedback Erases Evidence: Phase-Separated Completeness Auditing in Verus
abstract: Correctness feedback suppresses the very evidence that specification-completeness auditing is designed to uncover: programs that satisfy a written contract but violate intended behavior. We demonstrate this objective reversal on 12 Verus/Rust tasks across four model families under matched call budgets. Independent no-feedback discovery more than doubles certified-witness yield relative to IntentShield's corrective-feedback loop (59.0% versus 27.1%). A format-matched iterative control places the larger share of this gap in feedback content, not independent restarts. The advantage holds in every model family and survives parser repair. A separate phase-separated execution matches the aggregate yield without reusing responses; most certified witnesses also fail held-out cases. Preserving these witnesses delivers stronger specification repair: Phase-Revised contracts achieve 81.3% implementation success, versus 62.5% for IS-Revised, with Direct-Revised close behind. Both no-feedback witness sources substantially outperform weakened contracts. The effect does not reproduce in the available Dafny and Lean evaluations, establishing an empirical boundary around the studied Verus/Rust workflow. Completeness auditing and correctness repair have opposing immediate objectives. Preserve and certify the admitted failure before repairing it.

title: Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects
abstract: Conditional generative models are increasingly used for scientific prediction beyond the direct training support. Yet scientific questions often concern whether one intervention changes the effect of another. Such interactions can be of primary interest while explaining little of the total variation, allowing models to appear accurate overall without recovering the relevant scientific effect.
